approaches.name: Anterolateral approach to the distal tibia
approaches.corridor: Lateral to tibialis anterior with the anterior-compartment tendons and muscle retracted medially beneath the protected superficial peroneal nerve

sources.title: Anterolateral Approach To The Distal Tibia
Strategies for surgical approaches in open reduction internal fixation of pilon fractures
A systematic review of the role of surgical approaches on outcomes of tibial pilon fracture

procedure_applications.condition: Anterior or anterolateral articular injury and lateral metaphyseal comminution require direct reduction and buttress access
An extra-articular distal-tibia fracture is treated with an anterior-compartment submuscular plate

positioning.text: Position supine on a radiolucent table with a bump as needed, free ankle motion, and access for AP, lateral, mortise, and traction imaging.

setup.text: Use CT-based fragment mapping, confirm soft-tissue recovery, coordinate any fibular incision, and plan plate and distractor trajectories before incision.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark tibial crest, fibula, ankle joint, fourth metatarsal axis, superficial-peroneal-nerve course, and talonavicular joint.

incision.text: Center the incision on the ankle joint, aligned with the fourth metatarsal distally and midway between tibia and fibula proximally; limit proximal extension because anterior-compartment muscles arise from fibula.

superficial_interval.text: Raise full-thickness flaps, identify the superficial peroneal nerve where it crosses the incision, mobilize it, and open fascia beneath it.

deep_interval.text: Incise extensor retinaculum and retract the anterior-compartment tendons, including peroneus tertius, medially from syndesmosis, distal-tibial periosteum, and capsule.

layers.text: Skin, superficial-peroneal-nerve plane, anterior-compartment fascia/retinaculum, extensor tendons and muscle, capsule/periosteum, then plafond.

structures_encountered.text: Superficial peroneal nerve, extensor tendons, peroneus tertius, extensor digitorum brevis, anterior syndesmosis, capsule, distal tibia, and talar neck are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Superficial peroneal nerve, deep peroneal nerve and anterior tibial vessels medially, extensor tendons, anterior syndesmosis, fracture-fragment blood supply, and talar cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The superficial peroneal nerve predictably crosses the proximal incision; identify it before fascial opening and protect it throughout retraction and closure.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract the anterior compartment medially as a unit without excessive pressure on the deep neurovascular bundle or stripping articular fragments.

exposure.text: Provides broad anterior and anterolateral plafond visualization, reaches near the medial malleolus, and supports tibial and fibular fixation beneath robust lateral soft tissue.

limitations.text: Direct medial-joint access and proximal extension are limited by the anterior-compartment origin and neurovascular anatomy.

extensions.text: Extend distally toward talonavicular joint or elevate EDB for talar-neck distractor placement; avoid unnecessary proximal dissection.

indications.text: Use for many complete-articular pilon fractures, anterior/anterolateral partial-articular patterns, and selected extra-articular fractures requiring anterior plating.

relative_contraindications.text: Choose another corridor when the dominant pathology is medial/posteromedial, lateral soft tissues are compromised, or adequate skin bridges cannot be preserved.

implant_implications.text: Supports anterolateral buttress and submuscular bridge plates; place distractor rod posterolaterally so it does not obstruct reduction or implants.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Verify articular reduction, length, alignment, talar centering, plate position, and screw containment on AP, lateral, mortise, and oblique views.

closure.text: Repair capsule, retinaculum, and fascia without entrapping superficial peroneal nerve; close only when full-thickness flaps are viable and tension free.

complications.text: Complications include superficial or deep peroneal neuropathy, wound necrosis, infection, extensor adhesions, malreduction, nonunion, stiffness, and post-traumatic arthritis.

bailouts.text: Add a separate medial or posteromedial window when a key fragment cannot be reduced safely through the anterolateral corridor rather than stripping across the plafond.

questions.question: Which way are the anterior-compartment tendons retracted?
Why is proximal extension limited?
questions.answer: The anterior-compartment muscles arise from fibula and interosseous membrane.

approaches.name: Anteromedial approach to the distal tibia
approaches.corridor: Immediately medial to the intact tibialis-anterior tendon sheath with sagittal capsulotomy between anterior articular fragments

sources.title: Anteromedial Approach To The Distal Tibia
Strategies for surgical approaches in open reduction internal fixation of pilon fractures
A staged protocol for soft tissue management in complex pilon fractures

procedure_applications.condition: Medial and central plafond injury, medial-malleolar involvement, or varus-associated medial comminution requires direct access

positioning.text: Position supine on a radiolucent table with free ankle motion and access for orthogonal imaging and tibial-to-talar distraction.

setup.text: Delay definitive fixation until soft-tissue recovery is appropriate, map fragments on CT, preserve planned skin bridges, and plan medial/anterior plating before incision.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark tibial crest, tibialis-anterior tendon, ankle joint, medial malleolus, navicular base, and any traumatic wounds or prior incisions.

incision.text: Begin 5-8 cm proximal to joint just lateral to tibial crest and continue straight toward navicular base along the medial border of tibialis-anterior tendon.

superficial_interval.text: Raise a full-thickness flap without undermining adjacent skin bridges and expose the medial edge of the tibialis-anterior tendon sheath without opening it.

deep_interval.text: Incise periosteum just medial to the intact tendon sheath, develop the plane behind the sheath laterally only as needed, and open joint sagittally along the fracture interval.

layers.text: Skin, full-thickness anteromedial flap, periosteum medial to tibialis-anterior sheath, sagittal capsule, then medial/central plafond.

structures_encountered.text: Tibialis-anterior tendon sheath, anterior capsule, anteromedial and anterolateral articular fragments, medial malleolus, and talar dome are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Anteromedial skin flap, tibialis-anterior tendon and sheath, saphenous nerve/vein medially, anterior tibial vessels, fragment blood supply, and talar cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Do not violate the tibialis-anterior tendon sheath; repair any traumatic or inadvertent opening immediately to prevent tendon exposure beneath the wound.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid undermining the medial flap, forceful tendon retraction, or broad transverse capsular release that devascularizes anterior fragments.

exposure.text: Provides excellent medial and central plafond and medial-malleolar visualization with access to central/posterior impaction through fragment mobilization.

limitations.text: The far anterolateral Chaput fragment may require a separate small anterolateral window, and the medial soft-tissue envelope is vulnerable.

extensions.text: Extend proximally along tibial crest or add a separate limited anterolateral incision when direct lateral fixation cannot be performed safely through this corridor.

indications.text: Use for medial/central plafond injuries, medial-malleolar involvement, and varus patterns with medial comminution or buttress requirements.

relative_contraindications.text: Prefer an anterolateral or posterior corridor when medial skin is traumatized or dominant fracture fragments cannot be accessed without excessive stripping.

implant_implications.text: Supports medial or anterior plates and distal-to-proximal submuscular bridging; use a separate lateral window when screw trajectory requires it.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, mortise, and oblique views to verify joint congruity, restored alignment, talar centering, and extra-articular implant placement.

closure.text: Close sagittal capsule and periosteum, confirm the tibialis-anterior sheath is intact, and approximate viable full-thickness skin without tension.

complications.text: Complications include wound-edge necrosis, infection, tibialis-anterior exposure or adhesions, saphenous neuropathy, malreduction, nonunion, stiffness, and post-traumatic arthritis.

bailouts.text: Use a separate limited anterolateral window for an inaccessible Chaput fragment rather than extending beneath a tenuous skin bridge or tendon sheath.

questions.question: Which tendon sheath must remain intact?
Where is the preferred capsulotomy?
questions.answer: Sagittal, usually along the fracture interval between the main anterior fragments.

questions.question: Which pattern particularly favors this approach?
questions.answer: Varus pilon injury with medial comminution or medial-malleolar involvement.

approaches.name: Direct medial approach to the distal tibia
approaches.corridor: Direct subperiosteal medial exposure centered on a vertical medial split-depression fragment, with optional proximal MIPO extension

sources.title: Medial Approach To The Distal Tibia
Strategies for surgical approaches in open reduction internal fixation of pilon fractures
A systematic review of the role of surgical approaches on outcomes of tibial pilon fracture

procedure_applications.condition: A vertical medial split-depression fracture with medial articular impaction requires direct elevation and buttress fixation

positioning.text: Position supine with the leg externally rotated enough for direct medial access and maintain unobstructed AP, lateral, and mortise imaging.

setup.text: Confirm soft-tissue readiness, map medial impaction and osteochondral fragments on CT, and choose direct versus limited/MIPO plate application.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark medial tibial border, medial malleolus, ankle joint, saphenous vein and nerve course, and the proximal exit of the medial fracture line.

incision.text: Center the medial incision over the split fragment and extend proximally only enough to displace, reduce, and fix it or create a safe MIPO plate tunnel.

superficial_interval.text: Raise a full-thickness medial flap while identifying and protecting the saphenous vein and nerve.

deep_interval.text: Expose the vertical medial fragment directly, mobilize it enough to enter the joint, elevate adjacent plafond impaction, and preserve remaining periosteal attachments.

layers.text: Skin, saphenous neurovascular plane, medial periosteum, vertical fracture plane, then medial plafond and joint.

structures_encountered.text: Saphenous vein and nerve, medial tibial periosteum, medial split fragment, osteochondral fragments, impacted plafond, and talar dome are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Medial skin envelope, saphenous vein and nerve, periosteal fragment blood supply, posterior tibial structures with posterior extension, and articular cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Avoid placing bulky hardware directly beneath a compromised medial incision and avoid circumferential stripping of the split fragment.

retraction_hazards.text: Use limited atraumatic retraction; excessive flap tension or posterior dissection risks wound failure and neurovascular injury.

exposure.text: Provides direct visualization of a vertical medial split, medial plafond impaction, and associated osteochondral fragments.

limitations.text: Exposure is fracture-specific and does not adequately address dominant anterolateral or posterior plafond pathology through the same incision.

extensions.text: Extend proximally for direct medial plating only when soft tissues permit; otherwise combine limited articular exposure with percutaneous proximal plate insertion.

indications.text: Use for vertical medial split-depression pilon fractures with medial comminution, impaction, or an independent osteochondral fragment.

relative_contraindications.text: Choose an anteromedial or other fragment-directed approach when medial skin is tenuous or a plate directly under the incision would be unsafe.

implant_implications.text: A medial buttress plate may be applied directly or passed proximally using MIPO; position hardware to avoid incision pressure and saphenous structures.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, mortise, and oblique views to confirm elevation of impaction, medial buttress alignment, joint congruity, and screw containment.

closure.text: Restore periosteal coverage where possible and close the viable medial skin without tension or implant prominence beneath the incision.

complications.text: Complications include wound necrosis, infection, saphenous neuritis, symptomatic hardware, malreduction, nonunion, stiffness, and post-traumatic arthritis.

bailouts.text: Convert the proximal portion to percutaneous plate insertion or select a separate fragment-directed window if direct extension would compromise medial skin.

questions.question: What fracture morphology favors this approach?
questions.answer: A vertical medial split-depression fracture with medial articular impaction.

questions.question: What reduces proximal soft-tissue disruption?
questions.answer: Limited articular exposure combined with minimally invasive proximal plate insertion.
